E3 only describes the deposition method for the alloy in E2, providing no support for the hypothesis's key premises.
premises: Selective oxidation of CoCrFeMnNi during sliding wear forms a lubricious, self-healing oxide film in oxygen-rich conditions.
This oxide film reduces friction and wear by counteracting mechanical stresses.
In inert environments, the absence of this oxide film leads to higher wear rates.
The wear resistance mechanism is primarily governed by in situ oxide formation, not by other factors like subsurface grain refinement.
